description: God tells them to stop, look around, and ask for the old godly way. Then they answer Him. No, that's not the road we want.
excerpt: Most of the wrong turns I've made, I made at full speed. I already knew where I wanted to end up, so I wasn't really asking for directions. I was asking Him to bless the route I'd picked.
verse: This is what the Lord says: "Stop at the crossroads and look around. Ask for the old, godly way, and walk in it. Travel its path, and you will find rest for your souls." But you reply, "No, that's not the road we want!"
body_html:
God gives directions in this verse, and they turn them down. That's the part that stays with me.

He doesn't say hurry through the intersection and sort it out later. He says stop, look around, and ask. Most of the wrong turns I've made, I made at full speed. I already knew where I wanted to end up, so I wasn't really asking for directions. I was asking Him to bless the route I'd picked.

Then He says what's at the end of it. Rest for your souls. Not an easier road, not a faster one.

And they say no.

No, that's not the road we want.

They asked. He answered. They didn't like the answer, so they kept going.

I've done that. I've prayed about something I'd already decided on, and what I was really doing was looking for agreement. When the answer came back different, I told myself it wasn't clear yet and went the way I was going.

The old godly way is usually slower. It costs something up front. And it's the only road in this verse with rest at the end of it.

And He doesn't force them onto it. He tells them where the road is and where it goes, and then He lets them decide.

Most of us are standing at a crossroads about something right now. A decision at work. A conversation we keep avoiding.

He'll show you the way if you stop long enough to ask. The question is what you'll say when He does.

What crossroads are you standing at, and are you actually asking, or have you already picked the road?
question: What crossroads are you standing at, and are you actually asking, or have you already picked the road?
